roman-numerals-converter.html.intro_p: Roman Numerals use combinations of letters from the Latin alphabet (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) to represent values. Our converter handles large numbers up to thousands and covers both the additive and subtractive rules (like IV for 4) to ensure 100% accurate translations.
steps: Enter a modern number (e.g., 2024) to get the Roman Numeral instantly.
Or type a Roman string (e.g., MMXIV) to see the Arabic whole number result.
The tool validates your input in real-time, highlighting any invalid Roman sequences.
faq: What does 'M' stand for?
In Roman Numerals, 'M' represents 1000, 'D' is 500, 'C' is 100, and 'L' is 50.
Why is 4 written as IV?
Roman numerals use subtractive notation for 4 (IV) and 9 (IX) to avoid having four consecutive identical characters (IIII).
Is there a limit?
The tool can accurately convert numbers up to 3,999, which is the standard limit for traditional Roman Numerals.

Yes, completely free. You can use it for school assignments or artistic projects without any sign-up.

roman-numerals.html.intro_p: Roman Numerals originated in ancient Rome and remained the standard way of writing numbers throughout Europe well into the Late Middle Ages. This page provides a complete reference chart for common numbers (1-1000) and an interactive tool to convert any modern digit into its Roman counterpart.

faq: What is 2024 in Roman Numerals?
The year 2024 is written as MMXXIV.
Are there rules for Roman Numerals?
Yes, the most important is the subtractive rule: if a smaller value comes before a larger one (like IV), it is subtracted (5-1=4).
